html:
The Inca civil war was fought between two sons of Huayna Capac, Atahualpa and Huáscar, from about 1529 to 1532. Atahualpa, based in Quito, won, just as the Spanish landed.

Huayna Capac had spent his last years in the north, in what is now Ecuador, and died around 1527, probably of smallpox brought by Europeans. Huáscar ruled from Cusco, while Atahualpa held the northern army. War broke out, and the northern generals swept south, destroying the Cañari city of Tomebamba and capturing Huáscar near Cusco in 1532.

Atahualpa was on his way to Cusco when he met Francisco Pizarro and was captured at Cajamarca. The divided empire made the Spanish conquest far easier. In Ecuador, Atahualpa is remembered as a native son.
